key_findings.detail:
Na⁺ ions migrating through Mo accumulate preferentially at the CIGS/CdS buffer junction:

- Na concentration at CIGS surface increases from **$1.2 \times 10^{19}$ to $4.2 \times 10^{19}$ cm$^{-3}$** during PID stress
- Depletion region expands from **~500 nm to ~1.5 µm** toward the Mo back contact as acceptors are compensated
- Cation compensation reduces hole carrier concentration by **2–3×** from thermal effects alone at 85°C

- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=3|Theelen et al. (2018), p.3]]
- [[papers/MDPI-74-2828-2-s2.0-85078032594-2019-J-Influence of molybdenum back contact on the pid effect for Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells.pdf#page=4|Mansfield et al. (2019), p.4]]

At high ionic doses (21.1 mC/cm²), Na⁺ propagates all the way through the CIGS layer to the front TCO:

- Na segregates visibly at the ZnO:Al (front TCO) surface as white spots
- ZnO:Al layer is penetrated and partially demolished
- Na reacts with surface moisture/CO₂ to form sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) spots
- [[papers/MDPI-74-2828-2-s2.0-85078032594-2019-J-Influence of molybdenum back contact on the pid effect for Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells.pdf#page=5|Mansfield et al. (2019), p.5]]

Acceptor compensation by Na⁺ in the p-type CIGS reduces the built-in voltage ($V_{bi}$) of the p-n junction:

- Lower $V_{bi}$ reduces the maximum achievable $V_{oc}$
- This is the primary source of $V_{oc}$ degradation in CIGS PID (unlike FF-dominated shunting in c-Si)
- $I_{sc}$ remains relatively constant until advanced degradation stages
- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=4|Theelen et al. (2018), p.4]]

The degradation threshold and rate depend critically on the Mo back contact microstructure:

- **PID-susceptible Mo:** Degradation threshold ~2.7 mC/cm²; efficiency drops to 74% of initial at 21.1 mC/cm²
- **PID-stable Mo:** Threshold > 10× higher (> 27 mC/cm²); only slight Na increase in CdS at equivalent charge levels
- [[papers/MDPI-74-2828-2-s2.0-85078032594-2019-J-Influence of molybdenum back contact on the pid effect for Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells.pdf#page=3|Mansfield et al. (2019), p.3]]

key_findings.claim: Catastrophic Failure Timescale for Soda-Lime Glass Substrates
key_findings.detail:
CIGS on soda-lime glass (SLG) substrate shows extremely rapid degradation:

- After **25 hours** at −1000 V, 85°C: efficiency collapses from **14.9% to ~0%** (complete failure)
- This is far more rapid than c-Si PID because Na⁺ concentration in SLG is very high and the Mo-to-CIGS junction is the shortest possible path
- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=5|Theelen et al. (2018), p.5]]
